Build a project from what an instance serves: its lexicons, scripts, plugins and settings.

The project is read from the instance's live state, so dashboard edits are kept. A v3 instance is
read with your `hpy hv login` sign-in. A v2 instance needs --legacy and an API key with
lexicons:read, scripts:read, script-variables:read, plugins:read, labelers:read, users:read and
settings:manage (revoke it afterwards); each script is rewritten for v3 by the pinned HappyView's
happyview-codemod, and v2 plugins without an official registry project are left out. Script variable
values and plugin secrets are never pulled: the variables' keys go to .env.example, and the secrets
a plugin needs are listed. Ends by running `hpy hv check` on the new project, which is written
either way.

Usage: hpy happyview pull [OPTIONS] [DIR]

Arguments:
  [DIR]
          Directory to create, relative to the current one (default: one named after the instance's
          host)

Options:
      --json
          Print the result as JSON on stdout

      --url <URL>
          The instance, e.g. https://api.example.com (default: HPY_HV_URL, else the only one you are
          signed in to)

      --legacy
          The instance runs HappyView v2: sign in with an API key and rewrite each script for v3

      --no-input
          Never prompt; fail when a value is missing. Irreversible actions still need --yes. Implied
          without a terminal

      --api-key-env <NAME>
          With --legacy, the environment variable holding the v2 API key (default:
          HAPPYVIEW_API_KEY); without it, the key is asked for

  -C <DIR>
          Run as if started in DIR

      --diff
          Compare the instance with the project in DIR and print a unified diff; writes nothing

      --dry-run
          Print the files and the happyview.toml a pull would write, and write nothing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
